# 1 Clement Chapter 7 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 7 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_007_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 7

**7:1** These things, beloved, we write to you not merely for your admonition but also for our own reminder, for we are in the same arena and the same contest is set before us.

**7:2** Therefore let us abandon empty and futile reasonings, and come to the glorious and holy rule of our tradition.

**7:3** Let us attend to what is good and pleasing and acceptable in the sight of the one who made us.

**7:4** Let us gaze intently at the blood of Christ and understand how precious it is to his Father, because being poured out for our salvation it brought to the whole world the grace of repentance.

**7:5** Let us pass in review all the generations and learn that from generation to generation the Sovereign Lord has given an opportunity of repentance to all who desire to turn to him.

**7:6** Noah proclaimed repentance, and those who obeyed were saved. [Gen 6-8]

**7:7** Jonah proclaimed destruction to the Ninevites; but they, having repented of their sins, made propitiation to God through their prayers and received salvation, even though they were strangers to God. [Jon 3]

---

*LOGOS: "Sovereign Lord" for *despotēs* — Clement's preferred title for God, distinct from *kyrios*.*
